analysis.investment_thesis: Cyient is an engineering services company exposed to aerospace, defense, and utilities — all sectors I find genuinely interesting — but the growth story has hit a wall with FY25 revenue up only 3% and net profit actually declining from INR 703 Cr to INR 648 Cr. At forward P/E of 14.6x, the market is pricing in a recovery I'm not yet convinced is coming.
key_strengths: Genuine domain depth in aerospace, defense, and semiconductor engineering — these are high-barrier, long-cycle contract businesses where relationships compound over decades
Near-zero debt (D/E 0.07) and consistent positive OCF all 5 years, with INR 1,067 Cr cash on hand providing real financial flexibility
Forward P/E of 14.62x — if earnings recover 20–25% in FY26, the PEG drops toward 0.7x, which would be genuinely attractive by my framework
key_risks: Severe growth deceleration: revenue growth went from +32.7% (FY22→23) to +18.8% (FY23→24) to just +3% (FY24→25) — this is the most critical warning sign I look for
Net profit declined YoY in FY25 (INR 703 Cr → INR 648 Cr) — when earnings fall, the stock's story unravels faster than the numbers suggest
Operating margin compressed from 18.2% (FY24: 1,303/7,147) to 15.5% (FY25: 1,138/7,360) — revenue and margin contraction simultaneously is a double blow
red_flags: Finance costs have grown at 21.6% CAGR over 9 years, far outpacing revenue growth of 10.1% — cost structure is drifting in the wrong direction
Other income swung to -INR 2 Cr in FY24 after contributing INR 35–158 Cr annually in prior years — indicates FX losses or investment write-offs masking core business weakness
Revenue plateau at INR 7,147→7,360 Cr across FY24–FY25 suggests the major contracts driving the FY23–24 ramp are not being replaced at the same pace
analysis.detailed_analysis:
When I look at a company like Cyient, I ask: is this a temporary growth hiccup or a permanent deceleration? The 3-year revenue ramp from INR 4,534 Cr (FY22) to INR 7,147 Cr (FY24) was impressive — over 57% cumulative growth. But FY25's near-flat revenue and falling profits suggest those contract wins were one-time catalysts, not a sustainably expanding revenue base. The Design-Led Manufacturing segment and aerospace exposure are genuine strengths for India's defense indigenization story, but they haven't translated into numbers lately.

At 14.62x forward earnings, the market is essentially saying 'this is a turnaround candidate.' I might agree if management can demonstrate re-acceleration in H1 FY26. But I don't buy turnarounds until the turn has actually happened — I need to see earnings tick back up before I'd put new money to work. For now, existing holders should hold and watch the next two quarters closely; new buyers should wait for proof.
